scope: Native CLI lifecycle evidence for one synthetic JSONL source: declaration put/get/retry, activation put/get/state through initial selection, replacement, deactivation and reactivation, historical reads, stale and historical rejections, read-only store behavior and an unchanged query baseline. Every declaration get, activation get and state read, and every expected rejected administration write, is individually bracketed by a store fingerprint taken immediately before and after that command; query commands are not bracketed because they legitimately write policy decisions and trails. Deliberately an uncurated baseline: activation administration records a selection and enforces no suppression yet.
limitations: Not a retrieval-quality, semantic or performance measurement: the query observations only show which evidence identities and bytes the pinned revision still releases, and shared-host timings are not recorded.
The single synthetic source, three items and four transitions are a fixed fixture, not a sample of real curation workloads.
The actor, time and reason fields in the frozen events are recorded evidence, not authenticated authorship.

Storage checks are bounded: each administration read and expected rejection compares the canonical record tables, the supersession declaration, event and projection rows and the bytes of the main database file immediately before and after that one command. A WAL sidecar may hold committed transactions before a checkpoint, so this is evidence about those compared values, not a general integrity proof.
Accepted or live stores, MCP administration, older-store migration, damaged-store handling and enforcement are out of scope and were not exercised.
